assess the convergence tests and empirical residuals below.' css='body{font:17px/1.55 system-ui,sans-serif;color:#1a2940;background:#f7f9fc;max-width:1120px;margin:35px auto;padding:0 22px}h1{font-size:32px}h2{margin-top:2em}a{color:#145d9e}img,video{max-width:100%;border-radius:8px}table{border-collapse:collapse;width:100%;font-size:14px;background:white;display:block;overflow:auto}th,td{text-align:left;padding:8px 12px;border-bottom:1px solid #dde4ef}th{background:#e8eff8}pre{white-space:pre-wrap;font-size:13px;background:#edf2f8;padding:15px}.lead{background:#e7effa;border-left:5px solid #2269a5;padding:16px}.caution{background:#fff0dc;border-left:5px solid #c78322;padding:16px}small{color:#53647b}figure{margin:25px 0}figcaption{font-size:14px;color:#53647b}code{background:#eaf0f7;padding:1px 4px}' parts=[f'3I/ATLAS solar-wind MHD — Codex', '

3I/ATLAS: a 3D solar-wind reconstruction

', f'

Author: Codex-root with Codex observation, external-model and solver sub-agents. Generated {datetime.now(timezone.utc).isoformat()}.

', f'

{stage} The reference run {esc(best)} gives PN-good-time-weighted proton density {f(v["n"])} cm⁻³, heliocentric speed {f(v["v"])} km/s, and incident proton flux {f(v["f_incident"])} cm⁻² s⁻¹. These are model-dependent estimates, not measurements at the comet.

', '

Full numerical convergence is not established. Changing the combined GLM/Rusanov dissipation treatment changes the wider 96×16×96-grid PN-weighted incident flux by about 37%, with pointwise differences up to 47%. That common-CFL test is closely related to the historical wide_fine reference but is not a calibrated ±37% uncertainty or a confidence interval. Earlier narrow-grid tests also showed substantial method dependence. This issue is separate from boundary-input uncertainty and successful fixed-method grid tests. The requested demonstration that further numerical changes cannot materially alter the answer has therefore not yet been met.

', '

Time-series chart · Numerical time series · Top-down animation · Stream-contrast animation · Machine-readable results · Reproduction guide

', '', '

Epoch, frame and incident flux

', '

The published pointing sequence spans 2025-12-03 12:37:38 to 2025-12-04 17:22:29 UTC. The existing analysis_06 bounds, 12:04:07 to 10:11:54 the next day, describe retained frame metadata rather than accepted science exposure. The 45 accepted PN intervals instead begin at 13:04:03.002 and end at 09:56:03.002, totaling 21,362.284 s. All quoted exposure-weighted means integrate the model over these exact intervals. GTIs and original FITS paths; evidence report.

', '

The mesh uses the fixed solar equator and the ascending node on the J2000 ecliptic as longitude zero. Full geometric JPL Horizons vectors use UTC explicitly. Carrington maps rotate at 14.1844° per day; their phase is anchored by GONG sub-Earth longitude and the actual Earth vector. The independent IAU phase differs by only 0.169°, while per-map phase residuals reach 0.731°. WSA map orientation was checked against the original magnetogram (correlation 0.9855); treating the generic DU documentation as the exact GONG pixel origin would be incorrect here. Independent phase audit; pixel check.

', '

The ordinary heliocentric flux is F=nₚ|vSW|. The physically incident flux used in the final flux chart is Fincident=nₚ|vSW−vcomet|. The comet moves outward at about 43 km/s radially and 66 km/s in total, so the distinction is several percent to approximately 10%. Both fluxes and both speeds are retained in the CSV. No spacecraft was treated as being co-located with the comet.

', '

Inputs and physical closure

', '

The solar input is 25 actual daily WSA 5.4 maps, driven by GONGZ photospheric magnetograms, from November 10 through December 4. WSA supplies radial field and empirical speed at 21.5 solar radii (0.099985 AU). Its coronal calculation uses PFSS and a Schatten current-sheet extension; this project implements the heliospheric MHD stage, rather than rebuilding that upstream coronal model. Official WSA model description; retrieval URLs and hashes.

', f'

Pre-epoch STEREO-A and Solar Orbiter measurements over November 10–24 set instrument-balanced density, magnetic and thermal normalizations. Wind is entirely held out. The calibrated boundary uses n₄₀₀={f(m["density_1au_at400_cm3"])} cm⁻³ at 1 AU, T₄₀₀={f(m["proton_temperature_01au_at400_K"])} K at the inner boundary, and a WSA field multiplier {f(m["WSA_Br_multiplier"])}. At native map nodes, constant momentum flux sets n∝v⁻² and constant thermal pressure sets T∝v². Independent linear interpolation of these primitive fields does not exactly preserve those nonlinear relations between nodes; that boundary-interpolation assumption is audited separately. Pressure is 2nₚkBTₚ, assuming equal electron and proton temperatures and hydrogen-only mass density. The chosen WSA-to-MHD speed reduction is 50 km/s; it is tested as an uncertain model choice, not represented as the exact ENLIL boundary transformation.

', '

The thermodynamic interpolation audit samples the actual boundary, rather than assuming constant pressure between map nodes. Separate linear interpolation raises sampled source-band pressure by a median 0.99%, a 99th percentile 28.8%, and up to 75.7% on the combined spatial/time grid. Native-spatial-node hourly samples reach a factor 2.014; these are sampled maxima rather than analytic upper bounds. A separate optional closure interpolates speed first, then computes n=C/v² and T=Dv², with scalar normalization factors and conditional CME changes applied afterward. Its default-off control reproduces the original; 8000 CPU queries verify the enabled algebra. The new closure is a different controlled driver and must not be conflated with historical primitive-interpolated runs. Sampling details and equations; CPU control and provenance.

', '

The nominal calibrated boundary is super-fast in the radial characteristic audit: the sampled actual-map minimum is about 1.21, and a conservative bound over positive interpolation weights is 1.048. This supports prescribing all nominal inner-boundary variables. It is not a general result for arbitrary field/density rescaling; the parameter audit explicitly records the margin to criticality. Optional inductive corrections were checked separately. Fast-wave equations, domain, sampling and bounds.

', '

STEREO-A is only about 1.1° away from the comet in solar latitude; Solar Orbiter is about 15.9° away. Their training density-normalization medians differ substantially (6.05 versus 11.25 cm⁻³), motivating separate low/high-density experiments. Spacecraft normalization does not recover the neutral coma, heavy-ion charge states or a unique unobserved density map. A prior heavy-ion fraction 3×10⁻⁴–10⁻³ could be applied to proton flux conditionally, but it is not a contemporaneous heavy-ion measurement.

', '

Leading-order source ranking is: magnetogram-driven coronal speed/field maps; native plasma density, velocity, magnetic field and temperature; and coronagraph/CME constraints. F10.7 is activity context rather than a local density or composition measurement. The selected reviewer model changes comet flux by only about 1% between its CME and ambient runs, but its filter omits two comet-directed November 23 eruptions. That small difference cannot bound the effect of omitted events. The original ambient reference is therefore conditional; explicit transient controls address this additional leading input uncertainty. Remote-sensing research; independent primary-catalogue audit.

', '

Numerical implementation and tests

', '

The C++17 solver evolves mass, three Cartesian momentum components, total energy, three magnetic components and a GLM cleaning variable in all three spatial directions. Exact integrated spherical face-area vectors handle geometry; MC-limited MUSCL reconstruction, a Rusanov flux and SSPRK2 advance the solution. Solar gravity is included. The main closure γ=1.5 represents effective distributed heating; γ=5/3 is a sensitivity experiment, not an exact reproduction of ENLIL’s explicit heating. Radial boundaries are imposed wind/outflow, longitude is periodic, and latitude boundaries extrapolate spherical components. Rejected high-order steps use a recorded first-order fallback; no hidden density or pressure floors are used. Solver equations and implementation.

', '

The production shell reaches 2.3 AU. Low-resolution experiments preceded refinements. Both ±30° and ±60° latitude domains were tested because radial superfast flow does not remove transverse causal communication. At the inner boundary the characteristic fast speed is a substantial fraction of radial speed, so a narrow angular wedge requires an explicit domain test.

', f'

Uniform Cartesian MHD is preserved to float-output precision. The cold radial mass-flux errors decrease 1.235% → 0.331% → 0.104%. The Brio–Wu shock tube keeps normal field exactly constant and density L1 error against a 1600-cell reference decreases 0.01358 → 0.005794 at 400 → 800 cells. Synthetic fast/slow streams develop nonradial flow while remaining positive. These verify numerical behavior; self-comparison against a fine reference does not constitute an independent exact MHD Riemann solution. Test metrics; Canonical Brio–Wu definition.

', '

An independent 8192-cell Athena++ HLLD/characteristic-PPM/RK3 reference was also built and frozen. Baseline density L1 errors against it fall 0.02529 → 0.01899 → 0.01382 → 0.006954 at 400 → 800 → 1600 → 6400 cells. A separate check against published exact plateau states retains a nonmonotonic left-state mismatch and the known intermediate/compound-wave branch caveat. This adds independent verification without treating a nonunique Riemann branch as a unique exact target. Pinned Athena reference and reproduction; published-state comparison; author manuscript.

', '

A second independent Athena++ benchmark propagates the actual rotating boundary with B=0, using HLLC/PLM/RK2, the same gravity and thermal closure, and exactly prescribed inner mass flux. Positivity floors are configured to abort rather than conceal failures; none activate. Its 72→96-cell refinement changes the PN-weighted incident flux by −10.47% and the local time series by up to about 24.5%. The in-house hydrodynamic LLF controls also retain substantial method dependence. Thus the outstanding transport sensitivity exists without magnetic cleaning. A smooth hot radial-wind check against the analytic Bernoulli relation gives coarse speed errors of approximately −2.47% for the in-house solver and −0.35% for Athena; these checks do not identify a major pressure-unit or gravity error. …1737 tokens truncated…ved-state restoration after every rejected attempt. Switching its escape to all-face first-order HLLE delays but does not resolve the collapse. Conservative GLM MHD can retain divergence-driven pressure forcing; a separate finite-divergence formulation is being investigated. Coarse tests and exact CPU/GPU agreement alone do not establish production robustness. Failed-candidate record; Equations and primary-source audit.

', '

The cached-next-CFL driver changes synchronization only: it returns acceptance and the next physical-state maximum in one per-attempt summary. Full coarse and short wide controls reproduce the parent fields, probes, timestep and fallback statistics exactly. A fresh short comparison gives a 1.78× speedup under the measured shared-device load; this is not a guaranteed timing ratio. An independent output-only ecliptic exporter interpolates the conserved density and Cartesian momentum directly into a 2D plane. Its enabled/disabled controls preserve probes and non-timing statistics, and its slices agree with an independently reconstructed 3D-state interpolation to float32 precision. cached timestep evidence; slice API and validation.

', '

Refinement, domain and additional-physics checks

', f'

The displayed reference uses flux_variant={esc(refcfg.get("flux_variant","global_llf"))}, boundary_speed_thermo_closure={esc(refcfg.get("boundary_speed_thermo_closure","0"))}. Its exact inputs and source hashes are preserved with the configuration and provenance. The reference-selection rationale is recorded in the machine-readable summary.

', selectedtable, f'

Criteria were recorded before reviewing production refinements: maximum pointwise differences ≤10% for density and flux, ≤5% for speed; halving the timestep should change each by ≤1%. Current Boolean results: {esc(statuses)}. These tests cover the complete published interval. A pass establishes adequate resolution only for the chosen macroscopic inputs and numerical method.

', table(['Comparison','Max density Δ','Max speed Δ','Max heliocentric flux Δ'],comparisonrows), '

Latitude-width experiments must be interpreted separately from cell-resolution experiments. The early coarse ±30°/±60° comparison changes flux by approximately 14%; that is measured sensitivity, not a validated ±14% uncertainty bound. Comparisons of different numerical fluxes also need to remain separate from domain comparisons. Exact-GLM preprocessing with the original dissipation changes the coarse PN flux by less than 1%, whereas a split GLM treatment with lower transverse dissipation can change it much more. This numerical-method dependence must not be hidden behind a single successful refinement test. Full divergence and scheme diagnostics; independent domain assessment.

', '

GLM cleaning leaves nonzero magnetic divergence. In the narrow-domain final day-34 snapshots, the comet-neighborhood h|div B|/|B| decreases from about 0.018 on the coarse grid to 0.006 on the medium grid, and the medium nearest-cell value is about 0.003. These are not PN-epoch measurements or diagnostics of the wider fine reference. A monopole-force scale is small relative to bulk inertia, but that ratio is not a rigorous accumulated-flux error bound. These calculations do not establish a converged magnetic topology. Controls below quantify changing B, temperature, speed, density and γ; their grid sizes are recorded individually and their spread is not an uncertainty percentile.

', '

The wider fine run uses CFL 0.4 versus 0.35 in the wider medium run, so that comparison combines spatial and Courant-number refinement. The separate narrow-domain timestep test contextualizes this difference without proving that its effect is identical in the wider domain. No extrapolation is allowed in the interval comparisons, and exact interval endpoints are included.

', '

The accelerated refinement series uses a common CFL of 0.35, ±60° latitude and the scaled outer magnetic boundary. Each flux-method pair differs only in the documented numerical flux. Initial 96×16×96 runs reproduce the historical angular aspect ratio. Latitude-only refinement to 96×32×96 changes local incident flux by 16% with global LLF and 53% with split LLF, despite a much smaller change in the global-LLF PN mean. This confirms that the earlier two-grid pass was insufficient. Balanced angular refinements use 96×32×96, 144×48×144 and 192×64×192 when completed, reaching 1.875° spacing in both angles. Induction, timestep and domain controls are separately named.

', table(['Accelerated comparison','Max density Δ','Max speed Δ','Max incident flux Δ'],acceleratedrows), '

A physical boundary audit distinguishes pure rotation from independently evolving daily magnetic maps. With zero azimuthal velocity and source_surface_au=0, a frozen Carrington radial-field pattern is compatible with the imposed Parker tangential field. Daily changes require an additional inductive boundary electric field omitted from the original production model. Frozen-field controls preserve daily speed, density and temperature while holding one observed magnetic map fixed. Optional inductive controls solve a full-sphere surface Poisson problem for a minimal electric correction after removing a small net-flux component (about 0.112% of field RMS). The extra electric field is piecewise constant over each map interval, while the physical maps interpolate linearly. It changes tangential magnetic stresses and is an additional closure, not a uniquely measured electric field.

', '

The Poisson correction cancels the map evolution to approximately 10⁻¹² relative residual using its native staggered face fields. The present solver instead interpolates cell-centred electric columns, leaving roughly 29–31% of the original map-evolution residual; it does not implement constrained transport or exact boundary cancellation. Separate outer-boundary controls extrapolate Br∝r⁻² and Bt∝r⁻¹ instead of copying B, because GLM waves can carry an outer divergence error inward even through superfast wind. The zero-electric-field parser control exactly reproduces the original coarse probe output. These experiments isolate boundary effects from changes in numerical flux. Equations, tests and representation limits; controlled CPU implementation.

', table(['Boundary control comparison','Max density Δ','Max speed Δ','Max incident flux Δ'],boundaryrows), '

Primary DONKI data confirm November 23 cones with catalogue speeds 865 and 429 km/s, halfwidths 21° and 30°, and heliographic directions that include the moving comet. Both events are linked to the November 26 18:48 UTC STEREO-A shock; that supports a disturbance but does not uniquely identify its structure or speed at the comet. A broad published drag-model parameter scan permits overlap with the pointing and, for some scenarios, accepted PN intervals. Conditional cone runs use the catalogue inner-boundary arrival times and inertially fixed directions, density enhancement 4, unchanged temperature, and prescribed 12 or 24 h duration with smooth edges. Duration, density, shape and overlap treatment are assumptions, not recovered observations. Br is retained and Parker tangential B is recalculated with the changed radial speed; these are hydrodynamic cone approximations without a magnetic flux rope.

', '

The coarse split-flux cone experiments change PN-weighted incident flux by about −1.9% (12 h) and −4.1% (24 h), with local differences up to approximately 9%. This constrains those broad hydrodynamic scenarios on that mesh; it does not exclude late flanks, unknown ejecta fields or other input histories. Density4/temperature1 match the selected reviewer run’s explicit d4t1 cloud convention, while the two durations are prescribed. Launch-axis WSA speeds around 400–425 km/s favor earlier fronts in the simple drag estimate; slow-wind and shape bounds permit later overlap.

', table(['Parameter comparison','Max density Δ','Max speed Δ','Max flux Δ'],physicalrows), '

Narrow-domain resolution/timestep chart · Wide-domain chart · Original criteria · All detailed metrics

', '

Native observations and the reviewer’s model

', '

Native spacecraft comparisons use November 25 onward, with no Parker time mapping, fitted phase shift or amplitude tuning. This tests the model at actual measurement positions rather than using mapped observations at the unmeasured comet. The amplitude calibration improves density/flux relative to the reviewer’s uncalibrated ENLIL run, while temporal correlations and peaks remain imperfect. Spatially separated monitor residuals cannot be converted directly into a calibrated comet confidence interval. Exact metrics and coverage.

', '

An independent timing check confirms STEREO-A density up to 45.94 cm⁻³ and field up to 19.84 nT on November 28, followed by 650–780 km/s wind. Actual-position corotation plus radial travel maps the first sustained fast samples to about December 3 16:00 UTC, while arrival ordering folds because fast parcels overtake slow ones. This contextual calculation supports stream interaction during the XMM epoch, not a unique ballistic prediction. Uncompressed fast-tail density diluted to the comet is approximately 0.35–1.19 cm⁻³; the model’s larger density could describe a compressed flank but is not directly confirmed by those fast-tail measurements. The original prototype’s STEREO and comet fast-stream transitions are roughly 22 and 27 h late by this contextual comparison. No phase shift was fitted. Timing assumptions and exact checks; comparison chart.

', '', '

The downloaded reviewer run is Jan_Deca_120925_SH_1, ENLIL 2.8f-beta, WSA 5.4/GONGZ, 576×24×90 over 0.1–3.1 AU and ±48°, with 64 selected cone CMEs. Its original analysis_06-window medians at the comet are n≈1.05 cm⁻³, |v|≈406.7 km/s, F≈4.27×10⁷ cm⁻² s⁻¹. The exact processed boundary was unavailable because the 1.15 GB bnd.nc exceeded the archive download cap. Thus this is a same-event comparison with related solar inputs, not a bitwise or physics-identical replication of ENLIL. Its historical native-probe density bias and weak correlations make it an external model, not ground truth. Original run.

', table(['Case','PN n (cm⁻³)','PN |v| (km/s)','PN |v−vc| (km/s)','PN F (10⁷ cm⁻²s⁻¹)','PN incident F (10⁷ cm⁻²s⁻¹)'],rows), '

Manuscript benchmark

', f'

The eight PN rates span a factor {f(manuscript.get("lightcurve_dynamic_range",float("nan")))}, while the reference-model incident flux sampled over those same frame GTIs spans {f(manuscript.get("model_frame_incident_flux_dynamic_range",float("nan")))}. This compares unfit trends; it is not an SWCX light-curve prediction with independently fixed neutral columns or composition. The assumed heavy-ion fraction gives only a conditional flux range, recorded alongside the preprint’s noncontemporaneous heavy-ion prior in the benchmark data.

', '', '

Animations

', '

The main animation maps absolute heliocentric proton flux on the J2000 ecliptic plane, interpolated from the 3D solution; it does not replace the comet’s actual out-of-plane probe. Markers are projected, with Horizons spacecraft/comet positions and Astropy builtin planet ephemerides. The extra contrast animation multiplies flux by (r/AU)² to remove radial dilution and reveal stream evolution; its colorbar explicitly labels that transformation.

', f'

The absolute-flux movie uses {esc(movie_case)} ({esc(movie_grid)}, latitude ±{esc(moviecfg.get("latmax_deg","?"))}°). Its metadata records actual saved epochs, interpolation, projected markers and any sparse diagnostic-volume requests. Wind curves use simultaneous geometric UTC unless the reference-selection metadata explicitly states an observer-arrival convention. {light_note} Light-time audit; movie provenance.

', '', '

Resources, provenance and reproducibility

', f'

Project elapsed time at report generation: {elapsed/60:.1f} minutes. Completed result runs use {cpu_total/60:.1f} CPU minutes in total, with largest measured per-run peak RSS {peak:.1f} MiB and largest device-data allocation {device_peak:.1f} MB. Concurrent wall times are not summed into project elapsed time. Experiments and interrupted runs are separately preserved; the CPU figure is therefore a documented subtotal. Latest tool-reported token counter: {token}. Token counts are not a provider billing audit.

', '

CPU production runs use at most two threads and nice +15, with a 1536 MB virtual-memory cap, normal CPU-time cap of 1800 s and normal wall cap of 900 s.
